headline: Clean Max Enviro divests stakes in wholly-owned Vietnam and China solar subsidiaries via NSE-intimated share sale
sum: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions has sold its entire shareholding in two wholly-owned subsidiaries-Clean Max Muoi Private Limited (Vietnam operations) and Clean Max Chin Private Limited (China operations)-via stock-exchange intimation on 17 August 2026. Consideration and buyer identity not disclosed in the regulatory filing.
implication: Subsidiary share sales by listed renewable-energy companies trigger disclosure under SEBI Listing Rules Reg 30 even when consideration is immaterial; the strategic shift to exit or partner international solar operations signals a potential portfolio rebalancing or debt-reduction strategy in the renewable sector.
detail: Clean Max Enviro, a listed solar-energy developer, notified NSE of the sale of its entire shareholding in two wholly-owned subsidiaries: Clean Max Muoi Private Limited (engaged in solar operations in Vietnam) and Clean Max Chin Private Limited (engaged in solar operations in China). The transaction was disclosed as a Material Event intimation under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Neither the consideration amount nor the buyer(s) were detailed in the public filing, suggesting either non-material valuation or confidentiality undertakings in the sales agreement.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (Reg 30)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of material events including sale or disposal of assets/subsidiaries by listed entities; triggered this NSE intimation.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) – Schedule I & II
framework.note: Outbound foreign direct investment in Vietnam and China subsidiary repatriation; overseas remittance requires RBI/FEMA approval if consideration involves foreign currency.

framework.ref: Income-tax Act, 1961 – Section 32, Schedule VI (Capital Gains)
framework.note: Taxation of gains/losses on disposal of shareholding in overseas subsidiaries; capital gains treatment depends on holding period and treaty provisions (India–Vietnam, India–China treaties).
If disposal is part of a larger restructuring or scheme of arrangement, approval under s. 230 and NCLT sanction required.

framework.ref: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) Guidelines (if applicable)
framework.note: If either subsidiary holds renewable energy insurance or renewable purchase obligations (RPOs), portfolio transfer or novation may be required.

framework.ref: India–Vietnam and India–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA)
framework.note: Tax treaty provisions govern taxation of capital gains on sale of foreign subsidiaries and withholding obligations.

framework.ref: Ministry of Commerce & Industry – Foreign Direct Investment Policy
framework.note: Repatriation of funds from FDI in renewable energy ventures in Vietnam and China may require sectoral compliance checks.
